c1-plus-c2.tie_break:
within one Pareto front, and only there: acquisition cost plus the cost of running the WORKLOAD THE TASK DECLARES -- its own answer lengths -- both measured in wall time, then the earlier candidate in the grammar's fixed enumeration order. Stated here rather than decided per run.
Why this and not the cheaper acquisition: a probe at a small length measures the wrong thing. An acquisition is paid once and the saving grows with the length actually asked for, so a tie-break on acquisition alone would hand every task to the route that learns nothing, whatever the task goes on to ask. Both sides of the ledger are measured over the same declared workload instead.
This does not reintroduce a weighting across the Pareto components: it is one quantity in one unit, used only to order candidates that the frontier has already declared incomparable.
